title: Draft: eth: Make all MAC addresses show universal subfields (U/L, I/G, etc.)
description:
Make all FT_ETHER fields have universal subfields for the U/L, I/G
bits, the OUI, and the overall address (resolved and not) the way
that Ethernet source and destination addresses do, so that one can
filter for a MAC address appearing in any protocol (similar to e212).

Handle the case where the address does not appear directly in the
tvb but is calculated (such as DVB-DATA MPE), and use
TRY_TO_FAKE_THIS_ITEM_OR_FREE() to add the subfields even when
the item is faked so that filtering works properly.

This does not add specific subfields of "{field name}.lg" and
"{field name}.ig", only universal ones, so it is related to issue #15493
and issue #17246 but perhaps does not close them.

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • fae59589 - eth: Make all MAC addresses show universal subfields (U/L, I/G, etc.)
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/2524/diffs?diff_id=163015686&start_sha=3685b9b116e4b70b24c156ec43bb1490347ace81)

This is my least favorite approach of the three you mentioned in issue #15493. I think the FT_ETHER hook in proto.c has a bad smell and I really hope this MR is implemented in a different way.

If I had to put my finger on it it's because I don't think the zero-effort goal should makes us completely abandon the separation of concerns. This is unlike any other dissector API that I'm aware of and sets a poor precedent IMO.

Yeah, I don't really like this approach either. This was one attempt, but I'm not happy with how it turned out. I think that having the issue work would be nice, but I'm not sure of the best approach.

FT_ETHER is already kind of an odd case.
